A verdict that does not answer exactly what its brief asked records nothing; every record is verified on read — its run's proof verifies and it is what the run's draft concludes — and one that does not yields nothing. Runs briefed with `adjudication-brief/1` and `smoke-brief/1` keep verifying with their template.

**Delegated-review requests.** `pose review request <scope|bundle> --kind delegated-review [--purpose review|adjudicate|smoke] [--agents <name,...>] [--note-file <path>] [--apply]` opens an action request of kind `delegated-review` that binds the project, the worktree, the scope, the sealed bundle, the brief, the notes, the policies, the accepted agents and the destination of the conclusion (an attestation, an adjudication record or smoke evidence). No actor answers it: `pose action fulfil <act-id> --run <run-id> --runner agent:<id> --idempotency-key <key> --expected-revision <n> [--channel cli|ci|conductor] [--envelope <file>] [--apply]`, or the MCP tool `pose_action_fulfil`, submits a completed run, and the engine records the fulfilment only when the run is of the request's brief and bundle, of an accepted agent, completed with its containment, its signed proof verifies, its attempt ledger is intact and the engine recorded its conclusion at the request's destination; the fulfilment is verified again on every read. `pose delegate review <scope> --request <act-id>` runs the request's brief locally and submits the run once concluded. A rejecting run fulfils the request without approving anything; a superseded bundle or changed policy invalidates it, even once fulfilled, and it is asked again with `--supersedes <act-id>`, which retires it under the supersession authority rules (`--authority <json>`, `--role <role>`, `--requested-at` from the preview), or, when the plan now reserves the review for a person, makes the person's escalation its successor; a retry with the same key and run is a no-op. A person is asked by exception, as a decision request to the maintainer role: a plan that reserves the review for a person, a spent attempt budget, reviewers in conflict, and a `business_decision` a reviewer raised in its draft. A run's proof verifies in any checkout of the project: the worktree it ran in is recorded, not required of the reader, so a CI job or the Conductor fulfils the request with the same envelope.

Opt in to the verification bar with `delegated_review: true` in review policy only when preparing adoption. This live bar requires a signed run reference for agent different-actor review and refuses a prefix-only identity; it does not enable or add the future catalog capability. Non-adopting instances keep declared behavior. Under explicit executor-attested trust, normalized vendor OR model difference satisfies different-actor (vendor difference preferred); unknown baselines and the same vendor/model refuse. A machine run never satisfies mandatory-human. Catalog adoption, cutoffs/rollback and automatic conclusion application remain separate capability work.

Read the same current assurance through verify, review-check, MCP and `pose state --attention`: `machine-attested` names the signed executor declaration, its source, run/proof and vendor/model comparisons. Current issuer pins, project/audience/time, sealed inputs, retained artifacts and original/continuation receipts are reverified. Revocation, missing receipts, rewritten data or stale inputs remove machine assurance. Signing does not reset quotas or erase earlier rejecting runs. The origin worktree is recorded with the run, not required of the reader: a proof verifies in any checkout of the project, so a run a CI job or the Conductor performed is verified like a local one; no universal containment is claimed.

## CI failure interpretation

- Treat `POSE check (strict)` as merge-blocking on protected branches.
- Treat failed required checks in `POSE validate (strict)` as merge-blocking.
- Attach pipeline artifacts: `pose-check.log`, `pose-validate.latest.log`, and the POSE report.
- Classify optional-check failures as quality reservations with an owned remediation plan.
- Reject changes that violate specs, public contracts, security, or safe rollout.

## Phased rollout for unready modules

- Enforce the current required checks immediately.
- Use `moduleOverrides` to phase adoption without weakening global structural and required gates.
- Promote optional checks to required by module with an owner and agreed window.

### Optional-to-required promotion protocol

- Select a pilot domain and map candidate checks with owners and explicit risks.
- Measure success for four weeks and require a baseline of at least 95 percent.
- Promote only eligible domains through `moduleOverrides`.
- Update the validation matrix and quality policy in the same change set.
- Monitor regressions and adjust rollout without removing established required gates.
- Update specs and rules when rollout changes merge acceptance criteria.

## Definition of done

- Resolve or formally accept every critical and high finding.
- Make the final decision clear and actionable.
- Support quality and security conclusions with evidence.
- Preserve approved scope without unjustified drift.

## Reviewer mode

**Objective:** evaluate technical quality and production readiness with emphasis on correctness, risk, and scope.

- **Focus:** functional correctness, spec consistency, regression and security risk, operability, validation quality, and actionable feedback.
- **Anti-patterns:** approve without sufficient evidence; review style while ignoring functional risk; request unrelated changes; block progress on subjective preference.
- **Handoff:** state the decision, severity and evidence for each finding, safe merge or deployment conditions, accepted risks, and recommended monitoring.
# Rule: Security

## When to consult

Consult this guide for authentication, authorization, sensitive data, external integrations, dependencies, and attack surfaces.

## Required patterns

- Apply least privilege to resource and credential access.
- Store secrets only in appropriate secret-management mechanisms, never in code.
- Validate and sanitize external input for its execution context.
- Keep personal and confidential data out of plaintext logs and metrics.
- Evaluate new dependencies for maintenance, licensing, and known vulnerabilities.
- Test both positive and negative authentication and authorization cases.

## Blocking anti-patterns

- Committing credentials, tokens, keys, or secrets in any versioned artifact.
- Disabling TLS or certificate verification without a formally documented mitigation.
- Trusting client input for authorization decisions.
- Executing dynamic commands without adequate validation and escaping.
- Ignoring critical security alerts without an approved exception record.

## Minimum checks

- Run secret scanning on the changed diff or scope.
- Run the module's applicable dependency vulnerability scanner.
- Pass the relevant authentication and authorization tests.
- Complete a review for sensitive-data exposure in logs and configuration.

## Precedence in multi-domain conflicts

- Apply the most restrictive security, contract, and operational rule when domain rules conflict.
- Prefer verifiable check evidence and explicit risk mitigation when speed conflicts with control.
- Record the precedence decision and objective rationale in the review.

… `abandoned`. Do not invent labels such as `completed` or `100% COMPLETE`.
- Separate **implemented and verified** work from **planned or documented** work.
  A plan describes intent; do not present that intent as current reality.
- Reference the report or evidence that crossed the spec exit gate before using `done`.
- Convert relative dates to absolute dates and stamp the verification date.
- Declare exact source-tree artifact actions in the spec and reconcile them
  against an immutable Git change set before claiming delivery.
- Treat artifact declarations, Git observations and delivery verification as
  separate evidence; none proves the others by itself.
- For typed delivery targets, require a path from reconciled artifacts through
  a production entrypoint to current structured validation results. A surface
  requires reachability plus integration/e2e evidence; a composed capability
  requires integration evidence.
- Evidence answers for the component it ran in or for a component inside it: a
  module-wide run covers its subtree, but a result from a directory inside a
  component does not answer for the whole component. Coverage that rests only
  on a containing module is reported as `inferred-coverage` — name it as such.

## Blocking anti-patterns

- Claiming `100% COMPLETE` or production readiness without a green
  `pose validate --strict` for every affected module.
- Publishing contradictory delivery documents for the same scope; reconcile them first.
- Merging code with completion documentation before the applicable POSE checks pass.
- Mixing aspiration and verified state in one paragraph without clear labels.

## Minimum checks

- Run `pose check --strict` for structure and spec status enums.
- Run `pose validate --strict` for every module the document claims to deliver.
- Run `pose lint-spec` when the document is a spec.
- Run `pose artifact-check --strict` when the scope changes governed source-tree paths.
- Run `pose surface-check --strict` for specs with `delivers` and `pose
  roadmap-check --strict` before a roadmap claims completion.
- `pose assess discover --if-stale --update-state` when closing specs to update completeness metrics, technical debt, and reports under `.pose/assessments/` and `.pose/state/`.

## Precedence in multi-domain conflicts

- Prefer verifiable check evidence over progress narratives when rules conflict.
- When pressured to claim completion without a gate, record the real state
  (`in-progress` or `blocked`) and the remaining exit conditions.

Claude's stream repeats session_id in init and result events. The instance
profile selects the unique system/init event so the existing ambiguity guard
and private-session redaction remain intact. A restricted, noninteractive review
uses Read/Grep/Glob/Bash without Edit/Write/Agent tools or plan approval mode.
This changes neither independence nor stream/output/run limits; the actual
working tree remains checked for mutation. No vendor profile becomes a scaffold
default.

# handoff: pose-b34-implementation

## Context

B34 corrige a identidade de leituras de governança que não distinguia duas
edições sob uma árvore já dirty. A autoridade é a spec do motor POSE; a adoção
no projeto hospedeiro permanece fora do escopo. O ADR de views limitadas por
operação está aceito e o start nativo foi aplicado.

## Current state

Atualização de fechamento em 2026-11-06: o código `5c9f1a96` passou 189/189
checks; índice real, artifact-check e surface-check passaram. O check estrito
global seguinte falhou por agregação das closures de closeout e diagnósticos
em cascata. D7 e a emenda aceita no ADR definem coordenador auditado e views
limitadas por escopo; a investigação nativa `trn-78de82fe660bb649` está concluída
e o checkpoint da task `b34-d7-implementation` foi produzido com Sol medium. A task ficou interrompida por quota; a execução principal terminou os testes e ajustes. A seleção B34 ampliada passou com race (domínio 54,533 s, CLI 16,136 s, MCP 1,331 s), e scaffold/distpolicy passaram. A nova matriz completa e o check real ainda estão pendentes.
Consultar `report:2026-11-06-pose-b34-global-review-view-budget.md`. Ainda não há
bundle final, revisão Claude, atestação ou closeout. Os registros abaixo conservam
os checkpoints anteriores e não qualificam a correção D7.

`/home/go/IdeaProjects/harne8/.worktrees/pose-b34-recovery`, branch
`work/governance-read-view-recovery`, base publicada `7079eb86`.

O clone temporário desapareceu. Patches e saídas literais das sessões permitiram
recuperar o código, o ADR e este handoff. O plano recuperado está em `22f777e9`;
o novo start prospectivo está em `b2eb2d34`. Ele não afirma precedência sobre o
código recuperado. Os recibos históricos completos de start/amendments e os
commits `56f5c150`, `3565be8a`, `dcffc886` não foram transportados ou fabricados.

completa da recuperação aprovou domínio e MCP; a CLI teve duas negativas cuja
fixture usava modo 0444 como barreira contra substituição atômica. A recusa foi
movida para a fronteira real do publisher, preservando bytes e asserções de efeito;
os quatro controles positivos/negativos relacionados passaram depois da correção.
A matriz completa passou 189/189 em `f54e9285`. Esse resultado é histórico para
os patches posteriores, não aprovação atual. O índice real encontrou dois
limites que os testes anteriores não reproduziam: profundidade federada oito
aplicada a toda cadeia local e capacidade insuficiente para a operação completa.

   278	coordinator, every scope consumes the same pinned index generation, and its
   279	inputs (the federated material among them) are the same for every scope.
   280	D7 made each scope recompute them inside its own capture. With the
   281	pose-dist corpus as a federated dependency, the federated material of one
   282	harne8 check costs about 150 s and several hundred MiB of retained reads.
   283	Each of 16 workers recomputed and retained it: `pose check --tolerant`
   284	passed 10 GB within a minute, and four workers took 37 minutes.
   285	
   286	A scope operation created by a coordinator delegates its check of the
   287	consumed index's inputs to the coordinator operation. The bindings are
   288	computed once per (root, generation, producer), through the coordinator's
   289	Files and charged to its budget. The coordinator's final audit, which D7
   290	already runs after every scope joins, covers those reads. A scope's own
   291	closure keeps everything else it reads. An input that changes while the
   292	scopes run fails the coordinator's audit, so the gate fails: no scope is
   293	judged against a freshness check its closure does not cover. Measured on
   294	harne8: 248 s at a 2.5 GB peak with 16 workers, against an abort past
   295	10 GB.
   296	
   297	This shares one immutable answer (whether the consumed generation's inputs
   298	are current) in the binding-aware way D7 requires: scopes already prove the
   299	coordinator's authorized root vector before a capture. It does not make the
   300	scopes one snapshot.
